vam:O92636.summary: In the top register the Virgin lies on her deathbed surrounded by the apostles, St Peter swinging a censer and St Paul at the foot of the bed, while Christ stands behind the bier holding up a small figure of her soul, and angels descend to receive it. Below stand saints in two rows — Gregory of Nyssa and Basil, Peter and Paul embracing, and Cosmas and Damian, Nicholas and John Chrysostom — each identified by inscription. The plaque once formed the centre of a Byzantine triptych.
facts: The V&A places it in the so-called 'Nikephoros group' of Byzantine ivories, named after the panel on the Cortona reliquary of the True Cross associated by inscription with the Emperor Nikephoros II Phokas.
As frequently on Byzantine ivories, the back is carved with a large cross, here with rosettes at the ends of its arms.
The figure of the Virgin's soul held by Christ is a restoration (V&A).

vam:O92636.notes: Byzantine (Constantinople), late 10th or early 11th century. The Dormition is not narrated in Scripture, so no passage is given. Formerly in the Webb collection, acquired 1867.
